hunks.before: 2.1 Conservation is equivalent to constancy of $P$. By construction the set of values $x^1(p)$, $p\in\Omega$, is exactly the interval $J$ on which $\rho,P$ are defined. By step 1.1 and [F1], $T$ is conserved on $\Omega$ if and only if $P'=0$ at every interior point of $J$; by [F2] this holds if and only if $P$ is constant on $J$. The energy density $\rho$ is subject to no such condition: $\rho'$ never enters the divergence, because the only term containing $\rho$ is $T^{00}$, whose first index is contracted with $\partial_0$ and which is independent of $x^0$. [F2, step 1.1]
hunks.after: 2.1 Vanishing coordinate divergence and constancy of $P$. By construction the set of values $x^1(p)$, $p\in\Omega$, is exactly the interval $J$ on which $\rho,P$ are defined. The set $J$ is open: a chart ball about any point of $x(\Omega)$ permits all sufficiently small changes of its $x^1$ coordinate, hence a neighbourhood of each value in $J$ remains in $J$; this is also true when $J=\varnothing$. Thus every point of $J$ is interior. By step 1.1, $D=0$ on $\Omega$ if and only if $P'=0$ at every interior point of $J$; by [F2] this holds if and only if $P$ is constant on $J$. For nonempty $\Omega$, this is exactly local conservation by [F1]. For $\Omega=J=\varnothing$, $D=0$ and constancy of the empty function $P$ are both vacuous, with any real constant, for example $0$, witnessing constancy. The energy density $\rho$ is subject to no such condition: $\rho'$ never enters the divergence, because the only term containing $\rho$ is $T^{00}$, whose first index is contracted with $\partial_0$ and which is independent of $x^0$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]
